question:
Using dbt to build model in my databricks

As you can clearly see the inline macro dbt_utils function is not recognized. I did try creating a macro still getting this same error in the screenshot below.

not sure how to fix this error in dbt & databricks.

Code:

{{ config(materialized='table') }}
-- SCD 1
SELECT 
    {{ dbt_utils.sha2(['a.id', 'a.created_at'], 256) }} as dim_product_hkey
    ,a.id as product_key
    ,a.created_at
    ,a.title
    ,a.category
    ,a.ean
    ,a.vendor
    ,a.price
    ,1 as zzfl_current
    ,current_timestamp() as zzts_created
    ,current_timestamp() as zzts_modified
--FROM landing.products
FROM {{ source("landing", "products") }} a

Error:

Encountered an error: Runtime Error Compilation Error in sql_operation inline_query (from remote system.sql) 'dbt.context.macros.MacroNamespace object' has no attribute 'sha2'. This can happen when calling a macro that does not exist. Check for typos and/or install package dependencies with "dbt deps".

I know in dbt there is no built in SHA2, has someone cracked the SHA256 in macro code?
title: dbt_utils.SHA2() is not working in a macro
answer:
Solved the issue for the above problem. In DBT there is no OOB macro function like generate_surrogate_keys. Therefore I had to write a macro to do SHA256 with dynamic column lists.

Macro:

-- macros/custom_hasing.sql

{% macro generate_sha256_hash(separator, column_names) %}
    sha2(
        (
            {% for column in column_names %}
                coalesce(cast({{ column }} as string), '')
                {% if not loop.last %} || '{{ separator }}' || {% endif %}
            {% endfor %}
        ),
        256
    )
{% endmacro %}

Usage:

-- models/marts/dim/dim_product.sql

{{ config(materialized='table') }}
-- SCD 1
SELECT 
    {{ generate_sha256_hash('--',['a.id', 'a.created_at']) }} as dim_product_hkey    
    ,a.id as product_key
    ,a.created_at
    ,a.title
    ,a.category
    ,a.ean
    ,a.vendor
    ,a.price
    ,1 as zzfl_current
    ,current_timestamp() as zzts_created
    ,current_timestamp() as zzts_modified
--FROM landing.products
FROM {{ source("landing", "products") }} a

Hope this helps!
